title: Capability object manifest — objects.yaml
description:
REFERENCES ONLY. This file names object ids and never inlines an object. It sits beside capability.yaml so the load-set is readable without opening the capability, and so a change to what a capability loads is a one-file diff.

The core/scoped split is the point of the file. CORE objects are used by more than one capability and live in objects/core/. SCOPED objects are used by exactly one and live in objects/<capability>/. validate.py enforces the rule in both directions: a scoped object referenced by two capabilities is an error telling you to promote it to core, and a core object referenced by one is a warning telling you it may want demoting. Without that enforcement the distinction becomes a folder convention nobody maintains.

capability.description: The capability this manifest belongs to. Must match the sibling capability.yaml.

core.description: Shared objects from objects/core/. Authored once, referenced by many capabilities.

required.description: A missing one blocks the compile.

optional.description: Absence lowers confidence rather than blocking — Layer 3 strategy S8. A situation the compiler cannot fully feed should still produce advice at a lower confidence, not withhold it.

scoped.description: Objects specific to this capability, from objects/<capability>/.

never_load.description: Objects a situation must not pull in even if another capability in the same compile requires them.

load_order.description: Optional explicit order when one object's inference depends on another already being resolved — e.g. Budget before Qualification Score. Absent means order is irrelevant.
